cards.title: Shrinkage Impact on Individual vs. Simulation-Based Diagnostics
cards.claim: High standard deviation-based shrinkage (typically >20-30%) causes individual parameters (IPRED, IWRES) and Empirical Bayes Estimates (EBEs) to shrink toward population means, rendering individual-level diagnostic plots uninformative and obscuring covariate correlations. However, simulation-based diagnostics like VPC, pcVPC, NPC, and NPDE are not affected by shrinkage in the same manner and remain informative. Model selection should not be based solely on shrinkage; rather, shrinkage limits the reliability of individual post-hoc estimates for exposure-response analysis.
conditions: Applicable when evaluating mixed-effects models with sparse data or few observations per individual.
Shrinkage is calculated as SD-based; values >20-30% indicate high shrinkage.
Individual plots become less informative but are not inherently invalid if interpreted with caution regarding their reduced power.
required_inputs: Estimated individual parameters (IPRED, IWRES) and population predictions (PRED).
Calculated shrinkage values for random effects.
limitations: High shrinkage does not invalidate the model structure but limits the utility of individual-level diagnostics.
Shrinkage alone is not a criterion for model rejection; it indicates reduced information content in individual estimates.
External source status: FDA guidance is nonbinding; these are contextual guidelines, not mandatory project rules.
cards.downstream_use: Guide the selection of diagnostic tools: rely on simulation-based checks (VPC/pcVPC) when shrinkage is high; use individual diagnostics only when shrinkage is low or for specific covariate screening where shrinkage impact is assessed.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Residuals, VPC/pcVPC, convergence, uncertainty and external prediction diagnose different issues
